words.meaning: the proportion of total market sales made by one company or product
words.example: The brand increased its market share last year.

words.meaning: the amount of a product or service that buyers want and can buy
words.example: Demand for the service rises during the summer.

words.meaning: the amount of a product or service available to buyers
the situation in which businesses try to win the same customers
words.example: Competition encouraged the shops to improve their service.

words.meaning: a broad plan for achieving a long-term goal
words.example: Our strategy focuses on reliable service rather than low prices.

words.meaning: the amount of output produced for a given amount of work or resources
words.example: The new process improved productivity without longer working hours.

words.meaning: the ability to keep customers or employees over time
words.japaneseMeaning: 顧客や従業員の維持・定着

words.meaning: the process of obtaining goods and services for an organization
words.example: The procurement team compares offers from several suppliers.

words.meaning: the level of sales at which revenue equals total costs
words.example: The café reached its break-even point after selling two hundred meals.

sentencePractice.prompt: At this sales level, revenue exactly equals total costs, so there is neither profit nor loss. We are at the ____.
sentencePractice.reviewNote: Equal total revenue and cost uniquely identifies the no-profit/no-loss sales threshold.

words.meaning: a measure comparing the gain from an investment with its cost
words.example: The team estimated the return on investment before buying the equipment.
